name: Dido
notes: Cyrillic-based practical orthography for Tsez following the Avar-based Cyrillic convention used for unwritten Daghestanian languages of this area (Alekseev & Radzhabov's descriptions; Comrie & Polinsky's Tsez fieldwork materials). As in the already-registered Avar/Lak/Lezgian specs (av, lbe, lez), the Cyrillic palochka letter (I) combines with a base consonant letter to spell an ejective, pharyngeal or lateral series that a plain Russian letter cannot: kI/pI/tI/lI/khI/chI -- each such digraph earns its key because the combination's IPA is not the concatenation of the base letter's IPA plus a palochka sound (the palochka has no sound of its own; the whole digraph names one segment, exactly the lbe/lez/av convention this spec follows). gъ/къ/хъ/хь/гь mark the uvular/pharyngeal series the same way. Pharyngealization (a documented but non-universal Tsez feature on some vowels, Comrie & Polinsky) is not rule-encoded pending clearer minimal-pair citations; only the plain vowel readings are mapped. Stress in Tsez is not distinctive/predictable from spelling in the cited descriptions; left unset as a documented exemption.
